import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()
    
    # Sort by user_id, then event_ts, then event_id
    events = events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Extract date (calendar date in server local time)
    events["event_date"] = events["event_ts"].dt.date
    
    # Initialize session tracking
    events["session_num"] = 0
    session_num = 0
    
    for i in range(len(events)):
        if i == 0:
            session_num = 1
            events.at[i, "session_num"] = session_num
        else:
            prev_user = events.at[i - 1, "user_id"]
            curr_user = events.at[i, "user_id"]
            
            if curr_user != prev_user:
                # New user, start new session
                session_num = 1
                events.at[i, "session_num"] = session_num
            else:
                # Same user - check gap and date
                prev_ts = events.at[i - 1, "event_ts"]
                curr_ts = events.at[i, "event_ts"]
                prev_date = events.at[i - 1, "event_date"]
                curr_date = events.at[i, "event_date"]
                
                # Check if different calendar date
                if curr_date != prev_date:
                    # Different date - new session
                    session_num += 1
                    events.at[i, "session_num"] = session_num
                else:
                    # Same date - check time gap
                    gap_minutes = (curr_ts - prev_ts).total_seconds() / 60.0
                    if gap_minutes > 45:
                        # Gap > 45 minutes - new session
                        session_num += 1
                        events.at[i, "session_num"] = session_num
                    else:
                        # Same session
                        events.at[i, "session_num"] = session_num
    
    # Create session key
    events["user_session_key"] = events["user_id"].astype(str) + "_" + events["session_num"].astype(str)
    
    # Group by user and session to create user_sessions
    user_sessions = events.groupby("user_session_key", as_index=False).agg({
        "user_id": "first",
        "session_num": "first",
        "event_date": "first",
        "event_ts": ["min", "max"],
        "event_id": "count"
    }).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Flatten column names
    user_sessions.columns = ["user_id", "session_num", "session_date", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    
    # Ensure correct types
    user_sessions["user_id"] = user_sessions["user_id"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_num"] = user_sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_date"] = user_sessions["session_date"].astype("object")  # Keep as date object
    user_sessions["session_start"] = user_sessions["session_start"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["session_end"] = user_sessions["session_end"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["event_count"] = user_sessions["event_count"].astype("int64")
    
    # Sort output by user_id and session_num
    user_sessions = user_sessions.sort_values(by=["user_id", "session_num"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
